html:
A war in which Sparta conquered its western neighbour Messenia, dated by the later writer Pausanias to 743 to 724 BCE.

Messenia had some of the best farmland in Greece. The Spartan poet Tyrtaeus says the war lasted twenty years under King Theopompus, and that the Messenians held out on the fortified Mount Ithome. Later legends name a Messenian hero, Aristodemus, who sacrificed his own daughter to win the gods' favour, in vain.

When Messenia fell, its people became helots, tied to the land and forced to hand over half their harvest to Spartan masters. This gave Sparta the wealth to become the strongest state in the Peloponnese, but it also left it with a large, hostile underclass. The Messenians rose again in the Second Messenian War, and they did not win their freedom until 369 BCE, when Messene was refounded.
sum: A war in which Sparta conquered its western neighbour Messenia, dated by the later writer Pausanias to 743 to 724 BCE.
